cards.text: This one's a song, baker: a Psalm of Asaph, the man whose name is on it, set to a tune called The Lilies of the Covenant. Don't ask me to hum it, because my mustache starts flapping like it's trying to take off. Asaph opens with “Hear us,” and pictures God leading Joseph like a flock.

cards.question: Asaph pictures God's people as a flock. So what does he call God? O ___ of Israel
This Shepherd of Israel is also a King on a throne. Where does Asaph say God sits enthroned?

cards.text: Asaph asks God to shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh. That's not a quiet little prayer from the back, baker. That's a man standing on the counter going “OVER HERE!”

cards.question: Asaph has asked the Shepherd of Israel to shine forth. What does he ask God to do with His mighty power?

answers.text: Rally it and come save us
Hold it back a while longer
Turn it on the far mountains

cards.text: Then comes a line Asaph sings more than once, so lean in: “Restore us, O God, and cause Your face to shine upon us…” Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark junk drawer, so “shine upon us” hits me RIGHT here.

cards.question: Asaph asks God to restore them and make His face shine on them, so that they may be ___

cards.text: Now Asaph calls Him the LORD God of Hosts. And he asks the question every waiting person asks, the one I asked the dust in that drawer for years: how long?

cards.question: Asaph asks the LORD God of Hosts how long something will go on. What is it?

answers.text: His anger smoldering against their prayers
The famine spreading across the land
The war with the armies of Egypt

cards.text: Then Asaph describes what life has been like for God's people. Let's just say nobody's asking for seconds.

cards.question: What does Asaph say God has given His people to eat and drink?

answers.text: Bread of tears and tears to drink
Ashes for bread and bitter water

cards.text: And it's not just trouble at home. Asaph says God makes them contend with their neighbors, like a group chat where every single reply starts a new fight.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says their enemies are leaving them alone.
True or false: In Asaph's prayer, God has nothing to do with the troubles His people are facing.

cards.text: And here's that line again, with one addition: “Restore us, O God of Hosts, and cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.” Asaph's not done asking. Not even close.
Now Asaph changes pictures. No more sheep, baker, and I know, I was getting attached too. God's people are a vine, and Asaph tells its story from the day God uprooted it.

cards.question: Asaph says God uprooted this vine and moved it somewhere new. Where did God pull it up from?
True or false: Asaph says God transplanted the vine into empty land where no nations lived.

cards.text: God clears the ground for it Himself. Baker, I've cleared a LOT of countertops for a batch, but never a whole land.

cards.question: With the ground cleared, Asaph says the vine took ___ and filled the land

cards.text: This vine grows like dough you forgot about overnight. Its shade covers the mountains, and its branches cover the mighty cedars.

cards.question: Asaph's vine keeps on growing. How far does it send out its branches?

cards.text: Then the song turns. Asaph has a WHY for God, and it's a big one.

cards.question: True or false: Asaph says the people's enemies are the ones who broke down the vine's walls.
With the walls down, everyone passing by picks the vine's fruit. What comes out of the forest to ravage it?

cards.text: But Asaph doesn't stop at why. He turns it into a request and tacks on a “we pray!” Baker, when a man says please with an exclamation point, he MEANS it.

cards.question: What does Asaph ask the God of Hosts to do for the vine?

answers.text: Return and look down from heaven
Tear the old vine out for good
Plant a brand new vine instead

cards.question: Asaph reminds God this vine isn't just any plant. Whose right hand planted it?

cards.text: Then Asaph says it plain: “Your vine has been cut down and burned; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance.”
Then Asaph prays for one person: the man at God's right hand, the son of man God has raised up for Himself.

cards.question: Asaph prays, Let Your ___ be upon the man at Your right hand
Asaph asks God to revive His people. If He does, what will they do?
True or false: Asaph says that then the people will not turn away from God.

cards.text: Asaph closes with that line one last time, now with every title he's got: “Restore us, O LORD God of Hosts; cause Your face to shine upon us, that we may be saved.”

findings.problem: Joseph appears for the first time here, but Papa Dorin never says who he is. Joseph stands for God's people, and a baker could read him as the man Joseph.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh appear for the first time here, but the card never says who they are, for example tribes of Israel.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 6 cuts the refrain off with an ellipsis just before "that we may be saved". Card 7 then asks for the missing next word, so the baker is guessing how the line ends rather than reasoning about its meaning.

rule.text: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: "the one I asked the dust in that drawer for years" adds a new detail to the drawer backstory. In the backstory he counted the dust, went quiet and gave up. He never asked it "how long."

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Earlier cards already give the answer. Card 12 says "Asaph says God makes them contend with their neighbors," and the card 11 question says God gave His people tears to eat and drink. That leaves nothing for the baker to work out about whether God has anything to do with their troubles.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks for the exact word in "Let Your ___ be upon the man at Your right hand." Card 15 never showed this wording, and nothing lets the baker reason out "hand" over "crown." It tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "now with every title he's got" is not true. Verse 19 uses "O LORD God of Hosts," but earlier Asaph also called God "Shepherd of Israel" and "You who sit enthroned between the cherubim" (Psalm 80:1). Neither of those is in the closing line.

rule.text: **Noticing:** What he points out must be true.
